newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: ILO urges world pact against child labor.
newsitem.headline: ILO urges world pact against child labor.

text.p: The International Labour Organisation said on Friday it hoped countries all over the world would endorse a pact aimed at eradicating the worst forms of child labour by the year 2000.

The announcement was made by ILO director general Michel Hansenne at a meeting in this Caribbean port city focusing on the plight of at least 15 million children -- or one out of every five -- who are employed in some form of exploitative labour in Latin America.

The Geneva-based ILO first proposed the idea of a new convention on hazardous child labour, which would ban its most intolerable forms, in 1966. But Hansenne's remarks at the conference were believed to be the first time an actual time-frame was established for it to be adopted worldwide.
"Between 1998 and 1999, we are going to establish an international convention to eradicate the most intolerable forms of child labour," he said.
"We're already working to reach a consensus," he added.

In a speech to delegates and senior government officials from about 20 countries across Latin America, Hansenne said no government could look favourably on the fact that 250 million children were working in the world today, many of them in what he described as conditions of "extreme abuse."
"Child labour is a social illness that undermines social values and democracies," he said.

He added that the root cause of the phenomenon was poverty and that the liberalisation of world trade and globalization of the economy should ultimately work to alleviate the problem rather than make it worse.
"All countries should be making a sustained effort to guarantee that the poorest are beneficiaries and not the victims of economic change," Hansenne said.
